ANAND AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY (AAU) Department of Plant Pathology - Groundnut (■■■■■) Disease Advisory
1. Tikka Leaf Spot (Cercospora) and Rust Management
Groundnut Tikka disease produces circular dark brown to black spots with yellow halos on leaves, resulting in
premature leaf shed. Management: At first appearance of spots (usually 35-40 days after sowing), spray Mancozeb
75% WP @ 30-35 grams per 15-liter pump or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 25-30 ml per 15-liter pump. Repeat after 15
days if cloudy humid weather persists. 2. Collar Rot and Stem Rot (Sclerotium rolfsii)
Collar rot causes sudden seedling wilting with white mycelial growth and mustard-seed like sclerotia at the soil line.

Bio-fungicide Treatment: Apply Trichoderma viride @ 50-60 grams per 15-liter pump around root zones or mix 2.5 kg
Trichoderma with 500 kg well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM) per acre prior to sowing. Avoid excessive
irrigation that stagnates water around collars.

ICAR - CENTRAL INSTITUTE FOR COTTON RESEARCH (CICR) National Agricultural Advisory Bulletin: Comprehensive Cotton Health & Pest Management
1. Cotton Leaf Yellowing and Chlorosis Management
Leaf yellowing (chlorosis) in cotton is primarily caused by micronutrient deficiency, specifically Magnesium deficiency
or Nitrogen deficiency, often exacerbated by waterlogging. When veins remain green while interveinal areas turn pale
yellow or reddish (known locally as Lalio in Gujarat), foliar nutrition is urgent. Recommended Advisory: Spray
Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO4) @ 10 grams per liter of water (150 grams per 15-liter pump) along with Urea @ 10-15
grams per liter. Apply 2 sprays at 15-day intervals during flowering and boll development. 2.

ICAR_CICR_Cotton_Crop_Advisory.pdf_p1_c1.text:
Apply 2 sprays at 15-day intervals during flowering and boll development. 2. Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) Control Strategy
Pink bollworm is a destructive pest causing rosetted flowers and locule damage. Monitoring must begin 45 days after
sowing. Install pheromone traps @ 5 traps per acre with Gossyplure lures. If trap catches exceed 8 moths per night
for 3 consecutive days or 10% rosette flowers are observed, initiate chemical intervention. Recommended Spray:
Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 9-10 grams per 15-liter spray pump (200 g/ha) OR Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @
6-7 ml per 15-liter spray pump. Avoid continuous use of synthetic pyrethroids to prevent pest resistance. 3.

ICAR_CICR_Cotton_Crop_Advisory.pdf_p1_c2.text:
Avoid continuous use of synthetic pyrethroids to prevent pest resistance. 3. Sucking Pests (Aphids, Jassids, and Thrips)
Sucking pests infest the undersides of cotton leaves, draining sap and causing downward leaf curling, yellowing, and
stunted growth. Bio-control Action: Spray commercial Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Neem Oil (1500
PPM) @ 45-50 ml per 15-liter spray pump. Chemical Intervention: If pest population exceeds Economic Threshold
Level (ETL) of 5 nymphs per leaf, spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 4-5 ml per 15-liter spray pump or Thiamethoxam
25% WG @ 6-8 grams per 15-liter pump. 4. Agro-Chemical Safety and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Farmer Safety Protocol: Always wear personal protective equipment including face mask, safety goggles, rubber
gloves, and protective clothing.

ICAR_CICR_Cotton_Crop_Advisory.pdf_p1_c3.text:
Always spray in the direction of the wind; never spray against wind direction. Spray
strictly during cool hours (morning before 10 AM or evening after 4 PM). Strictly avoid banned compounds including
Endosulfan and Monocrotophos. Maintain a mandatory 15-day pre-harvest interval (PHI).
